# Why NLP, Why Now {#sec-why-nlp}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Chapter status: skeleton.**
:::

**Learning objectives.** After this chapter you can:

- describe what changed between 2017 and today that made language *the* interface to computation;
- place classical NLP, deep learning NLP, and LLMs on one historical map;
- name three problems in your own discipline that are now NLP problems;
- state what this course will and will not cover.

## Language became an interface

<!-- TODO(draft): opening narrative — from rule-based systems to statistical
     NLP to pretraining. One strong figure: a timeline. Frame for the

The shortest honest summary of the last decade: [text stopped being
unstructured data]{.hl}. Reports, logs, contracts, sensor annotations,
scientific literature — the material your field already produces — became
computable.
